doc.title: Ruth Brisbane interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 2, 2013

title: First professional job via Fritz Pollard and the missed Lionel Hampton chance
summary: Pollard's agency sent her to a New Haven club where Lionel Hampton offered an audition and Apollo job she missed.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Was there a certain age, when you were a teenager or whenever, when you were really thinking — well let me rephrase the question. Was there a point where you thought I could really make a living being an entertainer?

No. I was sort of like in limbo. I sort of dropped into singing. As I said, my sister-in-law sent me to a coach to get an act, AK, at a very good piano player and old football player. Let me think of his name. He had a booking agency on 125th Street. He sent me out to my
first professional job by an agent. He was a former football player. I’m sorry, Monk, it will come to me. Fritz Pollard.

Fritz Pollard. That was his name. He had an office on 125th Street. He sent me up to New Haven, Connecticut. I remember working there and getting the train from his office on 125th. And while I was working in this little black club up in New Haven, who comes in but Lionel Hampton. And he had me audition the next day at the theater he was working in. And I was so stupid. He said, “Stay and take the bus back with me, I want to talk to you about going into the Apollo with us.” But I already had my train ticket so I went home on the train, and when I went to the Apollo his band boy stopped me and tried to make himself into something else. You know what I mean. So I left. No nonsense. But anyway, I missed that opportunity working with Lionel Hampton. But I had opportunities that I didn’t even take, but I got dropped into music, that’s what I’m trying to say. It was nothing that I planned. Nothing that I planned.
It seems like I’ve heard stories about Lionel Hampton’s band boys somewhere else. Some people might not even know what a “band boy” is.
He wasn’t a boy, he was an older man. But I guess they see that everything’s running right, getting the musicians together.
You mentioned in passing almost that when you went to, was it New Haven you said, that it was a black club. Does that mean that white people couldn’t go there or just didn’t go there?
Oh, they went, they went. But it was black-owned and in a black area. Yes.
Dancing yes, and the band and an emcee singer. And the usual exotic dancers.
